exposure: use of four or more antiseizure medications
emergency room visits related to epilepsy
outcome: proportion of cesarean section (CS) among all deliveries
cohort: The study included women with epilepsy (WWE) and the entire female population aged 15-49 years in Korea.
finding: The annual childbirth rates declined more sharply and cesarean section (CS) rates increased more prominently in women with epilepsy (WWE) compared to the general population in Korea between 2004 and 2019.
mod_finding: The cesarean section (CS) rate was higher in WWE (51.2%) than in the general population (38.9%), and epilepsy severity and comorbidities (use of four or more antiseizure medications, emergency room visits, and Epilepsy-Specific Comorbidity Index >=2) were associated with increased CS risk.
